content.help: Riding speed as a percentage of your normal speed. Takes effect the next time you get on. Above about 350 the world may not load in fast enough.
Needs CMB_RiderPose.esp (make_rider_pose.bat). Off: you run in place over the bike. Takes effect the next time you get on.
Switch to third person when getting on, so you see the bike.

How steep a slope you can ride up, in degrees (on foot the game allows 47; 45 keeps a road bike off rock faces). Needs F4SE and the CMB_Slope.dll plugin. 0 = the same as on foot. Takes effect the next time you get on.
How far back the third-person camera sits while riding (the game's own is about 150). Needs F4SE and the CMB_Slope.dll plugin. 0 = leave the camera alone. Takes effect the next time you get on.

The tightest turn the bike makes at riding speed, in game units (about 70 = 1 m): no turning on the spot. Slower, it turns tighter (the next setting). Needs F4SE and the CMB_Slope.dll plugin. 0 = turn like on foot.
The tightest turn when the bike is barely moving; it widens to the turning radius above as you speed up. Needs F4SE and the CMB_Slope.dll plugin.
How fast the bike can be walked round when it isn't moving (and the least it turns at any speed). Needs F4SE and the CMB_Slope.dll plugin.

content.text: Caution (how early the bike eases off for obstacles, %)
content.help: 100: as the 2026-11-08a build (the throttle eases from about 11 m at full speed). Lower: closer to the obstacle before the bike eases off and stops. 60: from about 8 m, the throttle gone at 6 m. Needs F4SE and the CMB_Slope.dll plugin.

content.text: Bike tilts with the ground (max degrees)
content.help: While riding, the bike and the rider pitch with the ground by at most this much (needs F4SE and the CMB_Slope.dll plugin; 45 follows any slope you can climb). Takes effect the next time you get on.
Weapons and VATS stay usable while riding. Takes effect the next time you get on.
Shows the bike under you in first person (needs F4SE and CMB_Slope.dll). Takes effect the next time you get on.

content.text: Look down on getting into first person (deg)
content.help: Each time you go into first person on the bike, the view eases down this far so the dial and bars are in sight; look up whenever you like. 0 = the view left as it is (as before). Needs F4SE and CMB_Slope.dll.

content.text: Field of view riding in first person
content.help: The game's field of view while you ride in first person (more shows more of the bike, and widens the world too); back to yours as you get off or leave first person. 0 = your own, as before. Needs F4SE and CMB_Slope.dll.
Moves your seat in first person forward (+) or back (-), in game units. 0 = the plugin's EyeAt. At once.
Lower (-) brings the bike higher into view under you (its wheels lift off the road by as much in first person), higher (+) sinks it. 0 = the plugin's EyeAt. At once.
A big hit from an enemy knocks you off the bike, so you can fight back. Off: you keep riding; a hint says how to get off when a fight starts.

On: an enemy's power attack knocks you off whatever it costs you (the 2026-11-02a build). Off: a power attack is a hit like any other: it knocks you off only when it takes the Big hit share of your health. Explosions always do. Needs "Thrown off when hit".

Hits don't stagger you while riding (a stagger plays the standing animation, and the bike hangs round your hips). Explosions, and power attacks with "Power attacks throw you off" on, still knock you off with "Thrown off when hit" on. Off: staggered as on foot.

content.text: Pose re-check pause after a hit (s)
content.help: A hit, a stagger or an item used while riding can play a standing animation for a moment: that is a reaction, not the seated pose lost, so the pose isn't applied again for this long after one. 0 = applied again at any standing footstep, as before.

How much of your max health a hit (or several within about a second) must take to knock you off. Explosions always do, and power attacks with "Power attacks throw you off" on. 0 = any hit. Not in the first 3 seconds after getting on.

Hostile people, creatures and smaller robots the bike hits at speed are knocked over and take a little damage, and the bike loses some speed at each (needs F4SE and the CMB_Slope.dll plugin). Never companions, essential characters, anyone in power armor or the big ones (super mutants, behemoths, deathclaws, sentry bots, ...). Off: the bike brakes for them as for anyone.
How fast the bike must be going, in game units a second (riding speed is about 900 at Speed 250%). Slower, it brakes for them.
At riding speed; half that at the slowest, up to one and a half times faster. It takes their last point of health only with the setting below. 0 = none.

A knock-over that takes an enemy's last health kills it, and the kill is yours: quests and the rest as if you had shot it, and the experience with "Kill experience" below on. Never companions or essential characters (they aren't knocked over at all). Off: the bike leaves them at their last point of health.
What a kill by the bike gives you: 1 = the game's own experience, as for a kill of yours (the bike's last hit is yours); 2 = the same another way, should 1 give none; 0 = none, as before.
How much less fall damage you take while riding. 100 = none. Takes effect the next time you get on.

content.text: Free small falls (% of max health)
content.help: Falls while riding that would cost less than this much of your max health cost nothing. Bigger falls still hurt (less, by the setting above). 0 = off. Every fall while riding is logged.
On: the bike hangs off the seated rider, so it turns with you on the spot and in conversations. Off: it stays planted on the ground (the rider can twist on it). Takes effect the next time you get on.
Riding burns Flamer Fuel, from the side bag first, then your inventory.
In game units; about 70 units = 1 m. 21000 = about 300 m. Lower = thirstier.
Run alongside: they get the same speed boost. Ride along: they're hidden while you ride (riskier during their quests and scenes).
Companions running alongside further away than this are moved up behind you. 0 = never.
Pounds with F4SE (items without it). 0 = unlimited.
0 = silent. The engine follows it as you ride.
Landings and riding through water (the game's own sound files for now). 0 = none. The water follows it at once, a landing at the next one.

content.text: Bike sounds through the mod's own records
content.help: Landings and the water through the mod's own sound records over the game's sound files: heard at the riding camera's distance. Off: the game's own records, as the 2026-11-01a build (much quieter: they fade with the camera's distance and carry their own attenuation): the landings only with "Landing sounds without metal" off, the water only with "Water sound loop" on its first choice (the others are the mod's own records either way). Landings at once, the water the next time you get on.
How far under the hardest landing the softest one sounds. 10 by default; 18 as the 2026-11-01a build; smaller makes small drops louder.
On: a tyre thump, and on big drops a heavy dull thud under it; into water a splash, and on big drops a heavier one with a thud. Off: as the 2026-11-02a build, a metal clunk on big drops.
A tyre thump when the bike lands, louder the higher the drop, a heavier thud on big ones, a splash into water. Without F4SE one level.
Spray while riding through shallow water, by speed and depth (needs F4SE and the CMB_Slope.dll plugin). Takes effect the next time you get on.

Which water loop plays while riding through water. The first is the 2026-11-02a build's (the console's CMB_FxWaterPick); "Wet road, gentle" (since 2026-11-09a) is the mod's wet road with less hiss and more body. Takes effect the next time you get on.

content.text: Mute the rider's own jump and landing sounds
content.help: While riding, your character's own footstep, jump and landing sounds are silent (the bike's take their place). Takes effect the next time you get on.
The bike's headlamp (needs F4SE and the CMB_Slope.dll plugin): off, on while riding, or on at night (19:00 to 6:30). The hotkey below switches it while you ride.
Switches the headlamp while riding, until you get off or the next dusk or dawn; the setting above stays as it is.
The beam casts shadows (costlier: the game runs only a few shadow lights at once). Takes effect the next time you get on.
The tail lamp casts a small red light behind the bike, brighter while you brake (needs F4SE and CMB_Slope.dll). Takes effect the next time you get on.

A Customise button in the parked bike's menu: the field kit comes out of the side bag and you change the bike's badges, paint and mirrors at the armour menu. Off: no button, and the bike looks as it came.

Automatic uses an armour bench beside the bike, then the game's own armour bench if the first one's menu closes at once, and remembers the one that worked (its menu stayed open, or you made a change). The others force one: the toolbox ones are tests only (the game's toolbox can't be sat in).

options: Toolbox (a test: it can't be sat in)

content.help: Outside your settlements the field kit uses the side bag's components as well as yours. Off: only yours (and a settlement's workshop).
Crude wasteland humour and mild swearing among the plate texts at the field kit. Off: they aren't offered, and a plate wearing one shows its own text (at the next getting on, activation or Apply).

content.text: Free customising (no field kit, no cost)
content.help: Choose the look here instead: the choices below, then "Apply the look". No field kit and no components. Off: the choices are hidden, and the bike keeps the look it has.
The badge on the tank's left side (Stock: the winged wheel, as it came).
The badge on the tank's right side. "Same as the left" follows the left one.
A badge on the rear fender (None: as it came).
The tank's and fenders' paint and the coachline (Factory: the oxblood, as it came).
The colour of the Free colour paint, round the colour wheel (0 red, 120 green, 240 blue). Moving it chooses Paint "Free colour" when you Apply (or at the next getting on).
How deep or pale the Free colour paint is. Moving it chooses Paint "Free colour" when you Apply (or at the next getting on).
The stock mirrors, mirrors under the bars (egg or D), or none.
The wheels' style and finish (Stock: the cast wheels, as they came). Body colour follows the paint.
Black (as they came), whitewalls or a red line.
The licence plate's design (Stock: the plain plate, as it came).
The plate's lettering. "The plate's own" is the design's; the crude ones show as the plate's own while "Crude plate texts" is off.
The letters' colour ("The plate's own": the design's).
The plate's colour ("The plate's own": the design's).
Sets the paint, all three badges and, for some factions, the plate to one faction's when you press Apply.
Puts these choices on the bike now (the ridden bike at the next getting on).

content.text: Get on / off / call the bike
content.help: If you use this, set the built-in hotkey below to 0 so the key doesn't fire twice.
The F4SE hotkey that works without MCM. 48 = B, 34 = G, 47 = V, 0 = off. Press Apply after changing it.

Brakes while riding, as S does, and holds the bike still once stopped (S still backs up). A DirectInput scan code: 57 = Space, 42 = Left Shift, 29 = Left Ctrl, 56 = Left Alt, 45 = X, 46 = C, 0 = none (only S brakes). The log names the key it read. Takes effect the next time you get on.
Re-registers the built-in hotkey after changing it.
For alternative starts that skip the Pip-Boy: hands over the Motorbike Keys now.
Gets you off the bike and undoes everything riding changed: speed, controls, animations, hidden companions.
